skill.name: rust-cargo-assistant
skill.description: Guides Rust developers through Cargo project setup, dependency management, build profiles, testing, publishing, and common troubleshooting workflows.
skill.summary: Cargo-focused guidance for Rust project setup, dependency management, builds, testing, and publishing.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: The static findings were reviewed against SKILL.md and are documentation examples rather than executable code. Markdown fences, placeholder URLs, local path dependency examples, and privileged install examples do not show hidden automation, data exfiltration, or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Privileged package manager commands appear in troubleshooting examples.
remediation.suggestion: Add a note that sudo and system package installation commands require explicit user approval and should not be run automatically.

remediation.issue: Publishing and cleanup examples can modify registries or project files.
remediation.suggestion: Label cargo publish, cargo yank, rm, and cache cleanup commands as state-changing actions that require confirmation.

content.value_statement: Rust projects often need precise Cargo configuration, dependency updates, and build troubleshooting. This skill gives structured guidance for Cargo workflows in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains Cargo project initialization for binary and library crates.
Guides Cargo.toml dependency, feature, profile, and workspace configuration.
Suggests Cargo commands for building, testing, formatting, linting, and documentation.
Helps troubleshoot linker errors, version conflicts, slow builds, and cache cleanup.
Outlines crate publishing, versioning, package verification, and yank workflows.
Summarizes common Cargo ecosystem tools such as cargo-edit, cargo-watch, cargo-audit, and cargo-outdated.
limitations: It provides guidance but does not validate project files automatically.
It may suggest shell commands that require user review before execution.
It does not guarantee crate compatibility across every Rust toolchain version.
It does not replace security review for third-party dependencies.

use_cases.title: Set Up a New Rust Project
use_cases.description: Create a clear Cargo layout for a new binary, library, or workspace project.

use_cases.title: Maintain Dependencies and Features
use_cases.description: Plan dependency additions, feature flags, version constraints, and workspace dependency sharing.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Crate for Release
use_cases.description: Review package metadata, publishing checks, semantic versioning, and release maintenance steps.
use_cases.target_user: Library authors and open source maintainers

prompt_templates.title: Start a Cargo Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the right Cargo project structure for a new Rust command line tool. Include the first commands and files to create.

prompt_templates.title: Review Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Rust dependencies and explain which should be regular, development, build, optional, or feature gated dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Build
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me diagnose this Cargo build failure. Explain likely causes, safe checks to run first, and commands that need confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Release Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release checklist for publishing my Rust crate, including metadata review, packaging verification, versioning, and post-release maintenance.

output_examples.input: I need to add async support and JSON serialization to a Rust library.
output: Recommended dependency roles for async runtime, serialization, and optional features.
A feature flag plan that keeps default builds small.
A checklist for testing default, async, and full feature combinations.

output_examples.input: My Rust project builds slowly after adding many crates.
output: A diagnosis path covering dependency tree review, cache use, profile settings, and linker options.
Commands are separated into safe read-only checks and commands that change the system or project.
Tradeoffs for faster development builds versus optimized release builds.

output_examples.input: I want to publish a crate to crates.io.
output: A release checklist for metadata, readme, license, version, package contents, and dry-run publishing.
Warnings about token handling and irreversible publishing steps.
Suggested follow-up checks after the crate is released.

best_practices: Ask for project context before suggesting dependency changes.
Separate read-only Cargo checks from commands that modify files or publish packages.
Confirm privileged commands, package installs, and release actions before running them.
anti_patterns: Do not run publish, install, or cleanup commands without user approval.
Do not add broad dependencies or full feature sets without explaining build impact.
Do not treat example Cargo.toml snippets as final configuration for every project.

faq.question: Can this skill create a new Rust project?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide binary, library, and workspace project setup with Cargo commands and file structure advice.

faq.question: Can it edit Cargo.toml for me?
faq.answer: It can recommend edits and explain configuration choices. Actual file changes should follow the user request and project context.

faq.question: Does it run Cargo commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides command guidance. Execution depends on the host AI tool and user approval settings.

faq.question: Can it help with dependency security?
faq.answer: Yes. It references Cargo audit workflows and dependency review practices, but it does not replace a full security audit.

faq.question: Does it support Cargo workspaces?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workspace layout, shared dependency, profile, and multi-crate project guidance.

faq.question: Is it suitable for crate publishing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers package metadata, dry-run checks, versioning, publishing, and yank workflows.
